reader.requirement: At --std 85, a BLOCK CONTAINS ... CHARACTERS clause states the physical record size in character positions whatever the usage of the record's items; the physical record is implementor-defined and not visible to the program, so the compiler must accept the CHARACTERS phrase over records of any usage (DISPLAY, COMP, COMP-3, signed separate, variable length) and deliver every logical record unchanged and in order.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.DialectLevel >= 2002 gates the ordered-pair refusal COBOL2009 (2002+ SR1); at 85 the pair is not ordered
IntegerOperandRules.Classify/ZeroMessage by edition.DialectLevel: the nonzero rule and its citation (§1985:III.2 at 85)

reader.edition-search: grep BlockContains|FileDescriptionIdentity.Block over src (non-generated): the clause is read only by the binder, IntegerOperandPass and the external-agreement identity; no CodeGen or runtime member reads it, so the I-O path has no edition arm for it
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for this rule: the CHARACTERS phrase models nothing at any edition; the surrounding SR1 order check is 2002+ only
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f18_01 covers DISPLAY/COMP/PACKED-DECIMAL in CHARACTERS on sequential files; not a block smaller than the record, a RECORD VARYING file, SIGN SEPARATE items, or a relative file

reader.notes: The host's sequential and relative connectors have no physical blocking, so the CHARACTERS unit governs nothing observable; the compiler screens the integers and leaves the I-O unchanged, which every probe confirms across usages and organizations. Lead outside this rule: BLOCK CONTAINS 5 with neither RECORDS nor CHARACTERS compiles at --std 85, while the 1985 format prints {RECORDS | CHARACTERS} in braces (row 1985-FMT-VII.3.3.2; grammar makes the pair optional); not rendered from the PDF here.

refuter.evidence: Rendered PDF p397 (VII-23): the format is BLOCK CONTAINS [integer-1 TO] integer-2 {RECORDS | CHARACTERS} with RECORDS underlined and CHARACTERS not, so by §1985:IV.2.1.4 CHARACTERS is the implicitly selected default and BLOCK CONTAINS 7 alone means 7 CHARACTERS (the reader's lead that the omitted phrase under-rejects is wrong; accepting it is right). Probes at --std 85 under refute-1985-120/: blkrw.cob (report-file FD BLOCK CONTAINS 2 TO 132 CHARACTERS, and BLOCK CONTAINS 7 over an X(3)+COMP-3 record) exit 0, report lines 'ABC' twice, F6 XYZ -123 / PQR +045 read back; blkz2.cob BLOCK CONTAINS 0 TO 10 CHARACTERS and 0 TO 0 RECORDS each COBOL2386 (integer-1 zero refused too, not only integer-2); blkz.cob +2 refused COBOL0001/1970, 10.5 refused COBOL5506; blksd.cob BLOCK CONTAINS in an SD refused COBOL1970 (1985 SD format has no such clause).
